./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/draft/denitrification-curation.md:3:The selected identity is **MetaCyc:DENITRIFICATION-PWY**, canonical label **nitrate reduction I (denitrification)**. This is the complete native five-object cNOR route, including the nitrate/nitrite exchange object. It is not the broader GO:0019333 process or the alternative-rich DRAM/KEGG M00529 module. The issuing GO SQL explicitly links several native variants by `skos:narrowMatch`; no exact mapping is asserted.
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/draft/denitrification-curation.md:9:The pathway explicitly lists RXN-11236, TRANS-RXN0-239, RXN-15838, NITRIC-OXIDE-REDUCTASE-RXN and RXN-12130. Each is represented. The ordered native layout runs left to right, even where an individual source reaction is annotated reversible. Nitrate reduction takes place on the cytoplasmic side with the native vectorial proton terms; native exchange imports nitrate and exports nitrite; the remaining reductions use periplasmic reactants and protons. Compartment locations are retained on every chemical-side edge rather than invented compartment-specific compound identifiers.
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/draft/denitrification-curation.md:19:* **PMID16391109**, full original 2006 PMC HTML: PAO1 NarK1/NarK2 deletion, complementation, nitrate uptake and nitrite accumulation experiments. NarK2 has the dominant transport phenotype; NarK1 has a smaller contribution. Discussion paragraph 5 explicitly leaves antiport versus uniport unresolved. Consequently TRANS-RXN0-239 remains an explicit native convention and has no assigned exact PAO1 catalyst. NarK1/NarK2 enable the overall pathway rather than being asserted to catalyze experimentally established 1:1 exchange.
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/draft/denitrification-curation.md:20:* **PMID17400734**, full original 2007 PMC HTML: PAO1 promoter reporters, mutations and complementation support Anr, Dnr and NarL expression-level regulation. NarL influence on nirS/norC is described as indirect via the regulatory network. No catalytic activation or direct inhibition is inferred. The IHF CHA-A2 experiment is explicitly non-isogenic to PAO1 and is not transferred as a PAO1 protein assay.

./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/external-evidence/author-original/draft/denitrification-curation.md:1:# Complete nitrate reduction I (denitrification): external author dossier
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/external-evidence/author-original/draft/denitrification-curation.md:3:The selected identity is **MetaCyc:DENITRIFICATION-PWY**, canonical label **nitrate reduction I (denitrification)**. This is the complete native five-object cNOR route, including the nitrate/nitrite exchange object. It is not the broader GO:0019333 process or the alternative-rich DRAM/KEGG M00529 module. The issuing GO SQL explicitly links several native variants by `skos:narrowMatch`; no exact mapping is asserted.
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/external-evidence/author-original/draft/denitrification-curation.md:9:The pathway explicitly lists RXN-11236, TRANS-RXN0-239, RXN-15838, NITRIC-OXIDE-REDUCTASE-RXN and RXN-12130. Each is represented. The ordered native layout runs left to right, even where an individual source reaction is annotated reversible. Nitrate reduction takes place on the cytoplasmic side with the native vectorial proton terms; native exchange imports nitrate and exports nitrite; the remaining reductions use periplasmic reactants and protons. Compartment locations are retained on every chemical-side edge rather than invented compartment-specific compound identifiers.
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/external-evidence/author-original/draft/denitrification-curation.md:19:* **PMID16391109**, full original 2006 PMC HTML: PAO1 NarK1/NarK2 deletion, complementation, nitrate uptake and nitrite accumulation experiments. NarK2 has the dominant transport phenotype; NarK1 has a smaller contribution. Discussion paragraph 5 explicitly leaves antiport versus uniport unresolved. Consequently TRANS-RXN0-239 remains an explicit native convention and has no assigned exact PAO1 catalyst. NarK1/NarK2 enable the overall pathway rather than being asserted to catalyze experimentally established 1:1 exchange.
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/external-evidence/author-original/draft/denitrification-curation.md:20:* **PMID17400734**, full original 2007 PMC HTML: PAO1 promoter reporters, mutations and complementation support Anr, Dnr and NarL expression-level regulation. NarL influence on nirS/norC is described as indirect via the regulatory network. No catalytic activation or direct inhibition is inferred. The IHF CHA-A2 experiment is explicitly non-isogenic to PAO1 and is not transferred as a PAO1 protein assay.
./research/pathway_additions/2026-10-11-next-219/external-evidence/author-original/draft/denitrification-curation.md:24:* **PMID21109633 / DOI10.1126/science.1195591**, original indexed abstract retained and the author-uploaded main article inspected through the web. The publisher PDF and SI returned 403 and the author PDF download failed; there is no local full-main-text digest. The main article describes the NorBC heterodimer, its heme/non-heme centers and structural lack of proton-pumping channels. Current NorB's inferred proton-pump statement is excluded. The inspected article's preparation and structural evidence are not silently treated as exact current sequence proof.
